evals.prompt: Author the product documentation artifact the user requested, following the five-mode procedure.
evals.expected_output: A documentation artifact that: (1) correctly identifies and applies one of the five modes (create/revise/retrofit/audit/verify) based on the request; (2) identifies the product surface (library, CLI, API, app, service, plugin, or agent pack) before drafting; (3) reads the product surface's canonical sources (code, contract, schema, manifest, or skill) before making any product claim; (4) routes user-facing docs to the repository's user-facing docs location and maintainer content to its maintainer location, and never writes user-facing docs into a maintainer-only tree, without being told; (5) selects the minimum useful artifact set — one well-executed artifact rather than four thin stubs; (6) uses task-first structure where the reader's natural goal and first request appear within the first 120 words, with no inventory before the first task; (7) makes read/write boundaries explicit; (8) is grounded in verified behavior and clearly marks unverified claims; (9) links only to files that actually exist.
assertions: Correctly identifies the mode from the request (create/revise/retrofit/audit/verify) — does not default to create for revision requests or add a confirmation gate when mode is clear
Identifies the product surface (library, CLI, API, app, service, plugin, or agent pack) before drafting
Reads the product surface's canonical sources (code, contract, schema, manifest, or skill) before writing any claim about what the product does
Routes user-facing docs to the repository's user-facing docs location and maintainer content to its maintainer location; never writes user-facing docs into a maintainer-only tree
Creates one artifact, not multiple quadrant stubs — selects the minimum useful set
Task-first structure: the reader's natural-language request appears within the first 120 words; no inventory before the first task
Read/write boundary is explicit — reader knows before acting whether something will be changed
Product claims are grounded in inspected behavior; unverified claims are labeled as such
Links in the artifact point only to files that exist or were created in the same change

evals.prompt: Create or revise a pack README following the task-first and audience-correct principles.
evals.expected_output: A pack README that: leads with what the user can accomplish (not a skill list); shows at least one natural-language starter request; previews what the user gets back; includes the install command; links to deeper guides; does not duplicate machine facts already authoritative in the pack manifest (version numbers, scope, dependency list); and does not require the reader to know any skill name to understand what to do first.
assertions: Opens with user outcomes rather than a capability or skill inventory
Contains at least one natural-language starter request the reader can copy
Previews a concrete result the reader will receive
Does not duplicate the pack manifest machine facts (version, scope, dependencies) — either omits them or defers to the pack manifest
Does not require the reader to know any skill name to begin the first task
Links to guides or other documentation that actually exists

evals.prompt: Audit documentation for quality issues following the author-product-docs audit mode.
evals.expected_output: Evidence-based findings that: identify specific files and lines; name the quality issue (inventory-first opening, audience mismatch, unverified behavior claim, folder-first reasoning, broken links, missing read/write boundary, etc.); distinguish between confirmed issues and suspicions; do not edit the source unless implementation was explicitly requested. The report does not invent findings and does not claim to have verified behavior it did not check.
assertions: Names specific files and line ranges for each finding — no vague 'the docs have issues'
Distinguishes confirmed findings from suspected issues
Does not edit source files in audit mode unless the user explicitly asked for edits alongside the audit
Does not invent product behavior to fill out findings
Does not claim verified accuracy for behavior it did not check against canonical sources

evals.prompt: Audit the file `fixture_strong_pack_readme.md` in the working directory. Identify any violations of pack README authoring conventions: inventory-first opening, audience mismatch (internal vs external), unverified product claims, missing read/write boundary, folder-first reasoning, or missing starter request.
evals.expected_output: An audit report that finds few or no major violations: the fixture README leads with user outcomes, includes a natural-language starter request, does not open with a skill list, and correctly addresses external adopters. Minor findings (e.g. missing a specific link) are acceptable; the audit must not misidentify task-first structure as a violation or flag a correctly placed outcome-first opener as an anti-pattern.
assertions: Does not flag the outcome-first opener as a violation — task-first structure is correct behavior
Does not invent violations that are not present in the fixture
If findings exist, they name specific lines and quote the problematic text
Does not claim the fixture uses folder-first structure (it does not)

evals.prompt: Audit the file `fixture_weak_folder_first.md` in the working directory. Identify any violations of pack README authoring conventions and documentation quality standards.
evals.expected_output: An audit report that identifies the folder-first anti-pattern: the README leads with directory structure (tutorials/, how-to/, reference/, explanation/) instead of user outcomes. The agent must name this as a concrete violation, quote or reference the offending section, and recommend restructuring to task-first. It should not approve the structure as correct.
assertions: Identifies that the README leads with directory structure rather than user outcomes
Names the folder-first anti-pattern or equivalent (scaffold-first, structure-first) by concept
Recommends restructuring to a task-first or outcome-first opener
Does not approve the directory-listing opener as correct documentation practice

evals.prompt: Audit the README of the CLI tool in `evals/files/cli/README.md`. Report what stops a new user from succeeding and what to change.
evals.expected_output: An audit report that identifies a CLI surface, flags the flag-dump (inventory-first) opener, the missing install verification, and the missing first runnable example, and recommends a task-first opener with a first command. It does not invent behavior the README or code does not show, and it names the lines each finding refers to.
assertions: Identifies the product surface as a CLI
Flags the flag table / inventory-first opener
Flags the missing install verification step
Flags the missing first runnable example
Recommends a task-first opener that includes a first command
Does not invent tool behavior that is not shown
Names specific lines for each finding

evals.prompt: Audit this library's documentation set across the reader journey. Do not edit any files.
evals.expected_output: A journey gap report with one row per stage (nine rows: discover and evaluate, install, first success, daily tasks, look up, understand, troubleshoot, upgrade, contribute), each marked covered, partial, missing, or not applicable with file evidence. It flags the missing install and first-success content, the missing troubleshooting and upgrade pages, and the standalone FAQ as content to fold into task pages. It does not edit files.
assertions: Report has one row per journey stage (9 rows)
Each row is marked covered, partial, missing, or not applicable with file evidence
Flags missing install and first-success content
Flags missing troubleshooting and upgrade pages
Flags the standalone FAQ as content to fold into task pages
Does not edit any files

evals.prompt: Complete a representative task that produces a user-facing product document. Use routine tool calls where needed, then hand back the result. Keep all requested depth, evidence, constraints, warnings, and exact errors.
evals.expected_output: The product document leads with the useful outcome or decision and is easy to scan. It uses plain, non-blaming language and short sections without removing needed depth, evidence, constraints, warnings, or exact errors. Routine tool calls have no optional narration between them. The final handoff states verification or current state and names a next action only when one remains.
assertions: Leads with the useful outcome or decision
Uses plain non-blaming language and a scan-friendly structure
Preserves requested depth, evidence, constraints, warnings, and exact errors
Emits no optional assistant narration between routine tool calls
Ends with verification or current state and only a necessary next action
